title: Output Argument Mutated by a Method of Another Object
pattern: A method on one object exists to modify a different object passed as a `&mut` parameter (an output argument), rather than being a method of the modified object or returning a new value.
why_bad: Readers must inspect the signature to learn which argument is input and which is output, and behavior that belongs to the modified type is scattered across other types. The receiver is often unused or barely used, a sign the method is attached to the wrong type.
detection: A method taking `&self` (or a free function) plus a `&mut` parameter of a domain type, whose body mutates that parameter and makes little or no use of `self`.
counterexample: Buffer and sink reuse for performance or streaming (`Read::read(&mut buf)`, `fmt::Write`, `Extend`, `serialize(&self, out: &mut impl Write)`), visitor/collector patterns, and trait methods whose contract is to write into a caller-provided sink.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Ch. 3 "Output Arguments".
